predecessors.note: Across the civil war of 1799-1845: 'the islands were united into a Polynesian kingdom in 1845' by Tāufaʻāhau, who had held Haʻapai from 1820 and Vavaʻu from 1833.

capitals.name: Nukuʻalofa
capitals.note: Infobox 'Nukuʻalofa 21°8′S 175°12′W'; George Tupou I died there on 18 February 1893. The start year is this dossier's reading.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks: the whole Tongan group, 748 km2 (infobox), unchanged from the 1845 unification to today. The British protected-state years 1900-1970 do not change the shape (a vassal tint the British dossier should carry); the Lau claim in Fiji (1848-1868) is a vassal relation in the ledger, not part of this shape.

ledger.note: 1845: Tāufaʻāhau becomes Tuʻi Kanokupolu and unites Tonga as George Tupou I. Infobox 'Reign: 4 December 1845 - 18 February 1893'; he 'assumed nominal control over Tongatapu after gaining the title of Tu'i Kanokupolu in 1845', having 'received a dispute inheritance of land in Haʻapai in 1820' and 'gained control over Vavaʻu in 1833'. Tonga page: 'Unification c. 1845'. The land comes from the civil-war chiefdoms (nobody, in this map's terms).

region.text: the Lau Islands, where Ma'afu led 'the Tongan community' from Lakeba

ledger.note: 1848: Tonga claims the Lau Islands through Ma'afu. 'Ma'afu established himself at Lakeba as leader of the Tongan community in the Lau Islands in 1848'; he took Lau 'on the pretext that its chief had declared it Tongan', and 'In 1850, Enele Ma'afu gave the Tui Cakau a canoe' and received Vanua Balavu. The claim's standing is this dossier's reading, hence confidence 1.

region.text: the Lau Islands, where Ma'afu led 'the Tongan community' from Lakeba

ledger.note: 1868: Tonga disclaims sovereignty over Fijian territory. 'when the Tongan government disclaimed all sovereignty over Fijian territory', after which Ma'afu 'lost his authority as a Tongan prince over Lau'. The George Tupou I page dates it 1869: 'The parliament of Tonga agreed to end its claims to Fiji in 1869'. Lau continues as Ma'afu's Tovata (tovata-confederacy).

wars.name: Battle of Kaba
wars.outcome: Tongan victory for Cakobau; no change to Tonga's borders.
wars.note: 'Tupou defeated Cakobau's enemies at the Battle of Kaba in 1855.'

certainty.note: Island coasts throughout; the only soft element is the Lau claim of 1848-1868, which was a chiefly presence rather than a surveyed possession.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks entirely (no Tonga row at any date). Alive today: end is the current year. Vassal status: Tonga was a British protected state from the Treaty of Friendship of 18 May 1900 until 4 June 1970 (Tonga and History of Tonga pages); by the schema the suzerain records vassal_start/vassal_end, so british-colonial-empire (or whichever dossier carries the United Kingdom) should add 'vassal_start 1900 / vassal_end 1970, counterpart kingdom-of-tonga' (report: problems). Rulers: the pages opened give only George Tupou I (1845-1893), Tāufaʻāhau Tupou IV (1965-2006), George Tupou V (from September 2006) and Tupou VI (coronation 4 July 2015), not the reigns of George Tupou II and Sālote Tupou III, so the rulers key is omitted rather than filled from memory. The 1875 constitution (4 November 1875 coronation) is not a territorial event. Minerva Reefs (1972) are not on the pages opened. Native name is the infobox's usual form.
